title: Grade 5 Life Skills — Solving Everyday Problems Step by Step
subject: General Knowledge and Life Skills
description: Practice with questions on tradeoffs, planning, evidence, decisions.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Your group has 25 minutes and three tasks. Which first step makes the time limit useful?
choices: estimate task times and decide which tasks are essential
assign a task to nobody
start every task at once without a plan
save checking the clock for tomorrow

questions.question: Two bike routes take 12 and 18 minutes. The shorter route has heavy traffic; the longer has a protected lane. If safety is your top priority, which fits best?
choices: choose the route with the protected lane
choose the shorter route only because it saves time
leave the route undecided until halfway
choose neither until both routes take the same time

questions.question: Your class needs to know whether a change reduced trash. Which evidence is most useful?
choices: the name of the class
the color of the trash bins
trash counts before and after using the same method
one person's favorite snack

questions.question: A group disagrees about a plan. What helps find a workable decision?
choices: name shared goals and hear each option
let the loudest person end the discussion
keep the goals secret
choose a plan before stating the problem

questions.question: You cannot find the instructions for a project. What is a reasonable first step?
choices: copy a friend's finished project
buy supplies before knowing what to make
guess and submit without checking
check the class materials or ask the teacher for a copy

questions.question: A team needs supplies by Friday. One store is cheaper but delivers Saturday. If Friday is firm, what should the team do?
choices: order from both stores without checking money
wait until Friday night to look
choose the cheaper Saturday delivery anyway
choose a source that can deliver on time

questions.question: The first model fails. Which approach will best show what fixed it?
choices: change one part and test it again
assume the first model must have worked
throw away all test notes
change every part and skip testing

questions.question: You have $12 and need a $9 ticket plus a $5 bus fare. What is a sensible next step?
choices: buy the ticket twice
ignore the fare
buy both because 9 plus 5 is 12
find a cheaper way to cover one cost or save $2 more

questions.question: What is a useful backup plan for a picnic if rain is possible?
choices: buy more paper plates but keep the same plan
move farther from all shelter
reserve an indoor option or pick a rain date
check the forecast after the picnic

questions.question: Your teammate missed a meeting. What helps avoid misunderstanding?
choices: assume they already know every detail
share the decisions and check what questions they have
post a complaint about them
change all their tasks without telling them

questions.question: You have three tools and need to tighten a loose screw. What should you compare first?
choices: which tool is heaviest
which tool matches the screw
which tool has the brightest color
which tool was bought first

questions.question: A room gets noisy during group work. Which plan lets you see if a change helps?
choices: assume all groups make equal noise
ignore what the group thinks
try one noise rule and compare before and after
change the seating, schedule, and rules all at once

questions.question: You found a claim in an old post. Which step can check its accuracy?
choices: read only the title
compare it with independent sources and check dates
trust it because it has many likes
repost before checking

questions.question: Two assignments are due tomorrow. One needs a partner who leaves soon. What makes sense first?
choices: wait until both assignments are past due
switch between them each minute
finish the part that needs the partner
start the solo task and ignore the partner's time

questions.question: A team cannot carry all its equipment in one trip. Which plan checks the real limit?
choices: fill one bag before checking how heavy it is
check sizes and weights, then plan more trips if needed
leave the most important gear behind without asking
assume the lightest person can carry it all

questions.question: A meeting time works for all but one person. Which response seeks a fair solution?
choices: blame them before hearing the reason
cancel every future meeting
make a new rule that their ideas do not count
ask about a different time or a way for that person to contribute

questions.question: A lamp seems broken after a move. What is a safe first step for a child?
choices: plug it in if the cord looks torn
try exposed wires by hand
take apart the wiring alone
tell an adult and explain what happened

questions.question: A bag is lighter but holds fewer books. What does choosing it show?
choices: book weight no longer matters
a tradeoff between carrying weight and space
there is no difference between the bags
capacity always grows as weight drops

questions.question: After using a new schedule for a week, how can the group evaluate it?
choices: stop keeping track of work
assume it worked because it was new
compare what it finished with its original goals
judge only the page design

questions.question: Which question checks whether a proposed solution solves the right problem?
choices: What would we see if the problem were actually fixed?
What color should we make the title?
Can we stop asking questions immediately?
Who can take credit before we test?
